title: National Service Training Deaths and Safety Enhancements for the SAF
what_it_is: National Service Training Deaths and Safety Enhancements for the SAF

sections.label: Armed Forces Council COI convened
sections.summary: The Armed Forces Council convened a Committee of Inquiry on 25 January 2019, with all five members from outside MINDEF and SAF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: A COI has been convened by the Armed Forces Council (AFC) on 25 January 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: All five members of the COI are from outside MINDEF and SAF.

sections.label: ERPSS comments and SIB jurisdiction
sections.summary: ERPSS will comment on findings, which will be made public, and the SAF's Special Investigation Branch will investigate as Singapore authorities lack jurisdiction in New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The ERPSS will, in turn, provide its comments on the findings and both their comments and the findings will be made public.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: However, as CFC(NS) Pang's death occurred in New Zealand, neither the Police Force nor the State Coroner have jurisdiction for deaths outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Investigations to determine any culpability in this case will be left to the SAF's Special Investigation Branch (SIB) which has jurisdiction under military law.

sections.label: CFC(NS) Aloysius Pang at Exercise Thunder Warrior
sections.summary: CFC(NS) Aloysius Pang, aged 28, an Armament Technician, took part in Exercise Thunder Warrior at Waiouru Training Area in New Zealand this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: CFC(NS) Aloysius Pang, aged 28, an Armament Technician, was participating in Exercise Thunder Warrior at Waiouru Training Area in New Zealand this year.

sections.label: Cabin dimensions
sections.summary: The cabin is 2.3 metres high, 2.44 metres from front to rear, and 2.64 metres from side to side.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The cabin is 2.3 metres in height, 2.44 metres from front to rear, and 2.64 metres from side to side.

sections.label: Flick rammer position when gun lowered
sections.summary: When the gun is lowered, the flick rammer at the barrel's rear end goes up and ends about 10 centimetres below the cabin's top rim.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: When the gun is lowered, the flick rammer at the rear end of the barrel goes up and ends about 10 centimetres (cm) below the top rim of the cabin.

sections.label: CFC(NS) Pang caught in SSPH
sections.summary: CFC(NS) Pang was caught between the gun barrel and the SSPH interior as the barrel was lowered, sustaining compression injuries to his chest and abdomen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Unfortunately, CFC(NS) Pang was caught between the gun barrel and the interior of the SSPH as the gun barrel was lowered and sustained compression injuries to his chest and abdomen.

sections.label: Pang death after incident
sections.summary: CFC(NS) Pang died on 23 January 2019, four days after the primary incident, despite artificial life support and further treatment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Despite being placed on artificial life support and further treatment, CFC(NS) Pang passed away on 23 January 2019, four days after the primary incident in the SSPH.

sections.label: People inside SSPH cabin
sections.summary: CFC(NS) Pang, a Regular ME2 technician and a Third Sergeant NSman Gun Commander were inside the SSPH cabin when the incident happened.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: CFC(NS) Pang and one Regular technician of ME2 rank were inside the cabin of the SSPH with the Gun Commander, a Third Sergeant NSman, when the incident happened.

sections.label: Manual on lowering gun
sections.summary: The maintenance manual states the technician in charge must ensure the gun is lowered and fixed before maintenance works begin.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For the repair work in this case, the maintenance manual indicates that it is the responsibility of the technician in charge to ensure that the gun has been lowered and fixed in place before any maintenance works can begin.

sections.label: Operators' manual safety warning
sections.summary: The operators' manual contains a boxed, bold standard warning that failure to observe the warnings may cause serious injury or death to crew.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In the operators' manual, there is a standard warning, and I quote it, it is boxed in the Safety Manuals, printed in bold, quote, "Failure to observe the above warnings may result in serious injury or death to crew".

sections.label: No gun mechanism malfunction found
sections.summary: Inspections of the SSPH have not detected any machine malfunction of the gun lowering mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Inspections of the SSPH have not detected any machine malfunction of the gun lowering mechanism.

sections.label: SSPH training and firing figures
sections.summary: Over 15 years, more than 1,000 national servicemen and Regulars were trained on the SSPH and about 12,500 rounds fired.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Over the last 15 years, more than 1,000 national servicemen and Regulars have been trained to operate the SSPH, and about 12,500 rounds fired.

sections.label: COI recommendations on lapses
sections.summary: The COI will make specific recommendations to rectify any systemic or human lapses found.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The COI will also make specific recommendations to rectify any systemic or human lapses found.

sections.label: 42 SAR exercise at Jalan Murai
sections.summary: On 3 November 2018, 42 SAR conducted a two-sided company mission exercise at the Jalan Murai training area.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: On 3 November 2018, the 42nd Battalion Singapore Armoured Regiment (42 SAR) was conducting a two-sided company mission exercise at the Jalan Murai training area.

sections.label: COI findings on servicemen readiness
sections.summary: The COI found the servicemen qualified, rested per Training Safety Regulations, and mentally and physically fit, with no apparent effect on safety attention.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The COI determined that the servicemen involved were qualified to participate in the exercise, having undergone the requisite training for their roles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The COI was of the view that the servicemen involved had had their rest in accordance with the Training Safety Regulations, and that their mental and physical states were fit for participation in the activity and did not appear to have an effect on their attention to safety protocols.

sections.label: Land Rover stops short of safety distance
sections.summary: CFC Liu stopped the Land Rover behind the Bionix at most 19.8 metres away, short of the 30-metre safety distance, and four seconds later the Bionix reversed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Upon hearing the gunshots, CFC Liu stopped the Land Rover behind the Bionix and, based on the COI's calculations, this final position of the Land Rover would have been at a distance of "at most 19.8 metres from the Bionix, but short of the safety distance of 30 metres stated in the Training Safety Regulations." Four seconds after the Land Rover had stopped, the Bionix started to reverse as part of the extrication drill ordered by the Bionix vehicle commander, in responding to the shots.

sections.label: Bionix collides with Land Rover
sections.summary: About eight seconds after reversing, the Bionix collided into the Land Rover and mounted the driver's side before stopping.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Approximately eight seconds after it started reversing, the Bionix collided into the Land Rover and mounted the driver's side before coming to a stop.

sections.label: Extra e-horn buttons installed
sections.summary: Two more e-horn buttons have been installed in the rear of all Bionix vehicles used for training, in addition to the front button.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: First, in addition to the existing emergency horn (e-horn) activation button in the front for the vehicle commander, two more e-horn buttons have been installed in the rear of all Bionix vehicles used for training.

sections.label: Rear-view cameras for Bionix vehicles
sections.summary: From March this year, rear-view cameras will be progressively installed in the training fleet of Bionix vehicles so drivers can see when reversing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Second, from March this year, rear-view cameras will be progressively installed into our training fleet of Bionix vehicles, so that the driver can see during reversing.

sections.label: Safety table top exercises
sections.summary: The Army will now conduct safety Table Top Exercises for all high-risk non-live firing exercises before actual execution, as with live firing exercises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Third, as with live firing exercises, the Army will also now conduct safety Table Top Exercises for all high-risk non-live firing exercises before the actual execution.

sections.label: Medics upgrade emergency skills
sections.summary: Starting from March this year, medics will upgrade resuscitation and emergency handling skills through attachments to hospital emergency departments or ambulances.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Fifth, starting from March this year, medics will upgrade their skills in resuscitation and handling of emergencies through attachments to hospital emergency departments or ambulances.

sections.label: Dedicated safety unit at highest level
sections.summary: In response to recent NS deaths, SAF decided a dedicated unit will be set up at the highest level to drive and supervise safety culture and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Apart from these specific measures, in response to the recent NS deaths, SAF has decided that for the safety system as a whole, a dedicated unit will be set up at the highest level to drive and supervise a safety culture and enforcement against slack practices.

sections.label: SSRD expanded to Inspector-General Office
sections.summary: The Safety and Systems Review Directorate will be expanded and elevated to an Inspector-General Office under the Chief of Defence Force to oversee all Services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The current Safety and Systems Review Directorate (SSRD) will be expanded and elevated to an Inspector-General Office (IGO) under the Chief of Defence Force (CDF) to oversee all Services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Chief of Staff-Joint Staff (COS-JS), which is an existing appointment of a Service Chief equivalent, will concurrently be the Inspector-General.

sections.label: Safety lapses marked in performance reviews
sections.summary: Commanders of units that do not meet standards and have committed lapses in safety procedures and processes will have this marked against them in performance reviews.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Second, commanders of units which do not meet standards and have committed lapses in safety procedures and processes will have this marked against them in their performance reviews.

sections.label: Punishments for SAF safety lapses
sections.summary: An average of 2% of servicemen a year were punished under the SAF Act for safety lapses, with punishments ranging from fines to detention and administrative penalties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Over the past three years, an average of 2% of servicemen a year were punished under the SAF Act for safety lapses – 2 %.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Their punishments ranged from a fine to detention and administrative penalties, such as delays in promotion and reduction in benefits.

sections.label: 24-hour safety hotline calls
sections.summary: Servicemen can report safety incidents and near-misses through a 24-hour safety hotline, which receives about 140 calls a year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Servicemen can also report safety incidents and near-misses through a 24-hour safety hotline.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This safety hotline receives about 140 calls a year.

sections.label: National servicemen training fatalities
sections.summary: Four national servicemen passed away during training over the past 17 months, and the SAF had four training fatalities in 2012 but none from 2013 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Over the past 17 months, four national servicemen have passed away during training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In 2012, the SAF also experienced four training fatalities that year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But from 2013 to 2016, we had none.

sections.label: Accountability and safety timeout questions
sections.summary: MINDEF and the SAF will hold themselves accountable for every national serviceman, the speaker is sorry for four deaths, and questions were asked about the safety timeout for CFC(NS) Aloysius Pang.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: MINDEF and the SAF will hold ourselves accountable for every single national serviceman entrusted to us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I am deeply sorry for the loss of four precious national servicemen in the last 17 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With regard to the safety timeout called this time for CFC(NS) Aloysius Pang, how does this compare to the length of time of safety timeout called for previous training incidents, and whether there were any reasons for calling for a longer or shorter timeout?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I also understand that from 7 February, the safety timeout is progressively being lifted.

sections.label: Servicemen worried by recent incidents
sections.summary: Servicemen said they have served and know the SAF takes safety seriously, but are worried by four recent incidents, and the speaker welcomes rear-view cameras in the Bionix and five-tonners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Many of them prefaced their statement by saying that we have also served and we know that SAF takes safety seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But with four recent incidents, they are worried.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Lastly, I welcome the Minister's announcement that rear-view cameras, reverse cameras, will be installed in the Bionix as well as the five-tonners.

sections.label: Vehicle cameras and safety timeout lifting
sections.summary: A Member asked if cameras could be installed in all SAF vehicles, and the response said units on operations carry on while the safety timeout is lifted only for certain activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Although we go through vigorous training and ensure that there is always a vehicle commander or a safety officer to ensure that when we reverse these vehicles, there are occasions where lapses do occur and minor accidents do happen, fortunately not involving human lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, I do ask if SAF will consider installing these cameras in all our SAF vehicles eventually, so that it includes an additional safety element for the driver, on top of all the other safety features, as well as the vehicle commander and safety officers that we already practise today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Previously, there was a period and then units would revert back to their original activity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But as the Member rightly pointed out, after four deaths, old practices must be changed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, the difference is that units on operations carry on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We had a period of safety timeout, but it has been lifted only for certain activities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: More complex ones, more high-risk ones, CDF and his commanders want to be satisfied that not only are the training safety regulations in place, but that there is adequate behaviour, adequate culture in that unit, before you undertake them; and I fully support that.

sections.label: Training vehicles safety decision
sections.summary: They decided to apply the measure to training vehicles and are reviewing whether to also apply it to operational vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: With this incident, we decided that we will do it for training vehicles; we are reviewing if we should also do it for operational.

sections.label: Anyone can stop unsafe training
sections.summary: The speaker says everyone, including children, friends and relatives, and that anyone can stop unsafe training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It is all of us, our children, our friends, our relatives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I have said very clearly and in no uncertain terms that anyone can stop unsafe training.

sections.label: Safety breaches mark commanders' records
sections.summary: The Minister said commanders of units with safety breaches will have a mark on their record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister mentioned that for the commanders of units where there are some safety breaches, there will be a mark on their record.

sections.label: COI remit and systemic responsibility
sections.summary: The speaker asks when the Government would signal the entire Force about a systemic problem requiring a senior officer to take responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Moreover, each COI usually does not go beyond the remit of that particular incident in question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, at what point and at what stage would the Government think that it would be necessary to send a signal to the entire Force when they recognise that there may be a problem at the systemic or a greater level requiring a senior officer, whether at formation, army, SAF or beyond, to take responsibility on this?

sections.label: US Seventh Fleet commander relieved
sections.summary: In 2017, the US Pacific Seventh Fleet commander was relieved of command after four accidents involving the Seventh Fleet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2017, the US Pacific Seventh Fleet commander was relieved of his command after four accidents involving the Seventh Fleet.

sections.label: Senior leadership responsibility and population
sections.summary: The speaker says if senior leadership has to go for involvement or dereliction, the population will not stand for that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If senior leadership has to go because they have been involved or have been derelict, then I do not think our population will stand for that.

sections.label: Other armies zero training deaths
sections.summary: The passage asks whether other armies have achieved zero training deaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Are there any other models of other armies, for example, where they have been able to achieve zero training deaths?

sections.label: UK military training safety comparison
sections.summary: The passage states that over a 10-year period Singapore's safety records are slightly better than the UK's.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: There is a military that we can sort of compare our training with and, that is, the UK.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And over a 10-year period, our safety records are just slightly better than theirs.

sections.label: Re-employing retired officers as trainers
sections.summary: The passage suggests MINDEF consider re-employing retired officers and specialists to train NSFs and NSmen on risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As a suggestion, would MINDEF consider re-employing retired officers and specialists who have operational and safety experience to train our NSFs and NSmen on what risks to look out for prior to on-the-ground missions?

sections.label: Retired WOs extended service terms
sections.summary: The passage states retired experienced WOs are in short supply and their terms of service were extended.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But even that is in short supply – retired, experienced Warrant Officers (WOs), officers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And Members remember the Committee to Strengthen NS that we started up a couple of years ago where we wanted to put more trainers instead of national servicemen, we wanted to put those with the experience and that is exactly what we did.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We extended the terms of service for the retired WOs because they serve as a valuable resource.

sections.label: Rapid evacuation medical response limits
sections.summary: The passage states the SAF's medical response is rapid evacuation, which may not be adequate when evacuation is not prompt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Paragraph 6(b) states that the SAF's medical response is based on the concept of rapid evacuation to the next echelon of care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, such a response may not be adequate when a casualty cannot be evacuated promptly, as in CFC Liu Kai's case.

sections.label: Training Safety Regulation anyone can stop
sections.summary: The passage states there is a Training Safety Regulation that anyone can stop.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, recently, quite a number of mothers and grandmothers came to talk to me because their son or their grandson is going into NS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I think the reassurance is what the Members have asked in this House and what I have said, I stated very clearly there is the Training Safety Regulation that anyone can stop.

sections.label: Safety hotlines and real-time avenues
sections.summary: The passage states there are real-time avenues on the ground and safety hotlines for reporting recurrent safety lapses or risky behaviour anonymously.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, on the ground, there are avenues, that is, in real time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But apart from that, if there is a recurrent safety lapse or risky behaviour, we have safety hotlines which you can call anonymously or you can write and we will take action.

sections.label: Training cadre of grief counsellors
sections.summary: The passage states a request to train a cadre of grief counsellors with institutional memory to help others in similar vocation assist the bereaved.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This is an area which you want to retain people in and yet you hope that you do not need their services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And I have asked them to train a cadre of grief counsellors that can have institutional memory and that can help others in this similar type of vocation be able to assist those who have been bereaved.

sections.label: Time needed for information and facts
sections.summary: The passage states that if more information or facts are needed, the fullness of time will be given, normally two to four months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If they find that they need more information or facts, we will give them the fullness of time that they require.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But normally, as was the case with CFC Liu Kai, it takes a number of months, anything from two to four months.

sections.label: Commanders taken to task
sections.summary: The passage states that commanders will be taken to task if they ignore safety instructions or have a poor safety culture.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Commanders will be taken to task if they ignore safety instructions or have a poor safety culture.

sections.label: RSAF near-miss reporting
sections.summary: The passage states the RSAF had difficult incidents in the 1990s and now reports near misses for equipment and human error separately because solutions differ.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Some of you would remember that the Republic of Singapore Air Force (RSAF) in the 1990s had a spate of very difficult incidents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And today, the RSAF is a far cry from that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And that is exactly what they have incorporated, where they report near misses for equipment and near misses arising from human error.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: They separate them because the solutions are different.

sections.label: Surveys on training risks
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MINDEF or SAF would survey servicemen directly to sense training risks and be more aware of possible incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister: is there a way, whether MINDEF or SAF would, maybe go directly to the servicemen to do surveys to get an overall sense of training risks and then, from there, perhaps get to be more aware of incidents that could happen on the ground?

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And yes, there is much on the cards where you do safety audits, and you check and you have now hotlines that people can call in.

sections.label: Briefing on exercise manoeuvres
sections.summary: The COI asked whether the trainer and CFC Liu were briefed on expected manoeuvres, including a possible extrication drill, and left the first question to the Police.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, were the trainer and CFC Liu briefed on the expected manoeuvres during the exercise, including the possibility of an extrication drill happening?

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And for the first question why he asked him to move forward, it was not clear to the COI, and we have to leave it to the Police.
